**Differential Metabolomics Narrative — Arachidonic Acid Cascade Activation**

The seven differentially-abundant metabolites are strongly enriched in **arachidonic acid metabolism** (SMPdb SMP00075 / KEGG map00590). RaMP hypergeometric testing returned FDR = 0 with a fold-enrichment of ~735 across matched compounds, indicating a highly non-random convergence on this pathway. The six matched compounds — arachidonic acid (C00219), leukotriene A4 (C00909), 15-HETE (C04742), 5-HETE (C04805), 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ₂ (C14717), and 11,12,15-THETA (C14782) — represent three major branches of the arachidonic acid cascade: the lipoxygenase (LOX), cyclooxygenase (COX), and cytochrome-P450 (CYP) arms.

**Key drivers.** Arachidonic acid (C00219) is the shared substrate and the central node of the observed perturbation, with confirmed membership in SMP00075 (Arachidonic Acid Metabolism). KEGG reaction-path analysis confirms that arachidonic acid is metabolically connected to leukotriene A4 (C00909) via the intermediate 5-HPETE (C05356) in two hops (bidirectional), and is converted forward to 15-HETE (C04742) through a 15-lipoxygenase step (C05966). These three compounds represent the LOX arm (leukotriene branch) and the LOX/COX crossover product (15-HETE), collectively pointing to broad activation of lipoxygenase pathways.

**Biological significance.** Elevated leukotriene A4, 5-HETE, and 15-HETE suggest enhanced neutrophil and eosinophil chemotaxis, as HETEs serve as potent chemoattractants and leukotrienes mediate inflammatory cell adhesion and airway smooth-muscle constriction. The presence of 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ₂, a cyclopentenone prostaglandin with electrophilic reactivity, indicates a parallel COX-derived anti-inflammatory signal, as this prostaglandin acts as a PPARγ agonist to dampen NF-κB-mediated inflammation. The simultaneous elevation of pro-inflammatory leukotrienes and this anti-inflammatory cyclopentenone prostaglandin is consistent with a tightly regulated feedback response typical of acute or chronic inflammatory conditions.

**Upstream/downstream verified relationships.** KEGG path analysis confirms arachidonic acid → (5-HPETE) → leukotriene A4 (2-hop bidirectional path, indicating a reversible precursor relationship) and arachidonic acid → 15-HETE (2-hop forward path, indicating arachidonic acid as the upstream precursor). CDP (C00112) did not map to the arachidonic acid pathway and may represent a distinct metabolic perturbation. Overall, the data are consistent with a treatment-driven activation of the arachidonic acid cascade at the level of substrate mobilization and multi-arm enzymatic conversion, with downstream consequences for both inflammatory cell recruitment (LOX/leukotriene axis) and resolution signaling (cyclopentenone prostaglandin).
